text:
tina: monitoring alert — SCIM deprovision error rate spiked at 08:02 UTC, ~18% failures (lots of 403s) and several orphaned service accounts in audit logs. Anyone touch KMS or RBAC recently?
ben: I rolled an RBAC rename on the workspace->team mapping at 07:50. Didn’t touch KMS but we changed the service principal used by SCIM.
maya: @ben that will show up in KMS key policy checks if the principal ARN changed. paste the exact ARN you set?
ben: changed svcPrincipal: arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/scim-provisioner-v2 -> arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/scim-provisioner-v3
sam: grabbing scim-provisioner logs, see decrypt denies:  
```
2026-03-23T08:01:58Z ERROR scim-provisioner deprovisioner.go:142 "failed to decrypt extId" err="AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111222333444:key/abcd-ef01"
2026-03-23T08:02:03Z WARN  scim-provisioner deprov queue: failed-deprov item=svcacc-xyz reason=decrypt-failed
```
maya: that exact AccessDenied from KMS means the new role ARN isn’t in the key policy. So decrypts fail -> items get requeued -> end up as orphaned in the audit. KMS errors are opaque, we only get AccessDenied.
ben: damn, I forgot the key policy step. Could there be a cached policy issue after we update?
oncall-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1378 "SCIM deprov KMS access denial causing orphaned service accounts" — paging eng-security & eng-platform
maya: triage plan: 1) add new role ARN to KMS key policy allow list 2) restart scim-provisioner to clear cached KMS contexts 3) run backfill for missed deprovisions 4) audit logs window to quantify gap
sam: I can update key policy. suggested snippet to append: 
```
{
  "Sid": "AllowScimProvisioner",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": ["arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/scim-provisioner-v2","arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/scim-provisioner-v3"]},
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey*"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```
maya: keep v2 for a 48h grace window while the rollout finishes, then prune. also scope via Condition to our account or a tag if possible.
sam: pushed key policy update at 08:12 UTC and verified with get-key-policy — both ARNs present.
```
$ aws kms get-key-policy --key-id abcd-ef01 --policy
# output shows AllowScimProvisioner with v2 and v3 ARNs
```
maya: next step restart scim-provisioner pods (staging then prod) to flush cached KMS contexts.
sam: rolling restart now -> kubectl rollout restart deployment/scim-provisioner -n platform
oncall-bot: k8s: deployment/scim-provisioner restarted (rolling) — pods cycling
ben: after restart retries succeed, sample logs: 
```
2026-03-23T08:15:25Z INFO  scim-provisioner deprovisioner.go:180 "decrypt succeeded" item=svcacc-xyz
2026-03-23T08:15:27Z INFO  scim-provisioner deprovisioner.go:205 "deprovisioned user" u=svcacc-xyz
```
maya: good. run a backfill for the outage window (07:45–08:12) and validate zero failures. sam?
sam: running backfill: tools/scim backfill --since 2026-03-23T07:45Z --batch 200. first batch: processed 7 previously failed items, 0 failures. continuing.
tina: audit note: 08:00–08:06 shows KMS entries with missing correlation ids — file a follow-up to tighten correlation logging between SCIM and KMS calls.
maya: action items: 
- ben: document RBAC rename checklist + include explicit KMS key policy update step (assigned)
- eng-platform: add CI lint that flags ARN changes vs key policies (assigned)
- eng-security: review audit retention & ensure KMS logs include correlation ids (assigned)
- SRE: add temporary alert for KMS AccessDenied spike from scim-provisioner (assigned)
ben: opened GH issue #5825 with checklist + link to this thread
sam: created post-incident runbook PR with exact commands and rollbacks used during the fix
oncall-bot: incident INC-2026-1378 resolved -> root cause: RBAC principal rename not added to KMS key policy. remediation: updated key policy, restarted scim-provisioner, ran backfill. follow-ups filed.
tina: can we add a staging test that simulates principal rotation and verifies decryption flow before rotating in prod?
maya: yes — will add to eng-platform backlog. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
